title: Power-torsion kernel embeds in a deep ideal quotient
statement: For a map b:Q -> R of coherent modules on a Noetherian scheme X and an ideal K, if K^t ker(b)=0 for some positive t, then for some n the composite ker(b) -> Q -> Q/K^(n+1)Q is a monomorphism.

source.place: Tag 01YA (Artin-Rees), applied to the uniqueness argument of Tags 0889 and 088A

proof.text: The kernel T of b is coherent by coherent kernel closure and hence quasi-coherent by the coherent/finite-type criterion. Apply the existing sheaf Artin-Rees inclusion to T -> Q: for e >= c, T intersect K^e Q is contained in K^(e-c) T. Set e=c+t, which is positive. The right side is zero by hker. The kernel of T -> Q/K^e Q is this intersection, so this map is monomorphic. Write e=n+1. This uses the uniform sheaf Artin-Rees theorem, whose finite-affine-cover argument is already recorded in its own node.

theorem coherentMap_torsion_completion_ext_zero
    {X : Scheme.{u}} [IsNoetherian X] (K : X.IdealSheafData)
    (Q R : CoherentModules X) (b : Q ⟶ R)
    (hker : ∃ t : ℕ, 1 ≤ t ∧
      IsZero (Scheme.idealModuleProduct (Scheme.idealSheafPower K.toModulesι t).2
        (kernel b.hom))) :
    ∃ n : ℕ, Mono (kernel.ι b.hom ≫ formalModuleQuotientπ K (n + 1) Q.obj)
